judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare dollar figure for eligible employees; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 3.A.2) (c010) exactly at $35,000. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same lump-sum/annuity election as Attachment A, with 'prevailing market interest rates' and 'a major insurance carrier' left unquantified. The mis-typed 'annucy' is transcription noise, not substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Attachment A, II.2 (c038) and is consistent with 3.A.2) (c010); no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The estate rule is clear on its face, but the closing sentence subordinates it to 'the terms of the annuity' without saying how far. That is a modest nameable tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Notice of Termination form appended to Attachment B directs the remaining buyout amount to a named individual, not the estate, which pulls against this paragraph in the same attachment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single plain undertaking; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to Attachment A, II.4 (c040); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite 45-day period, only 'promptly' left soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c015 and c044 and with the reorganisation triggers in paragraphs 5 and 6 (c020, c021).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The eligible class is defined only as those 'to be identified on Attachments "1" and "2"' — a class fixed by documents that do not accompany the text, with the future tense leaving identification incomplete. That is a nameable indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix A, D (c057) then extends guarantees to Eligible Group I Employees 'who obtain guarantees pursuant to paragraph 4B,' persons by definition not on Attachments 1 or 2; the class definition here does not accommodate them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Guaranteed the opportunity to work five straight time shifts per week' is the classic ambiguity between a guarantee of work offered and a guarantee of pay, and 'guarantee period' is set only by the following paragraphs. Both are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4.C (c018) frees The Times from replacing absent RSHs and 4.D (c019) lets it consolidate segments, both of which can bear on whether five shifts per week are in fact offered; Appendix A, C (c056) and E (c058-c061) further qualify the guarantee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Effectiveness turns on 'completion of the process described in paragraph 4B,' but 4B describes a replacement process running 'during the term of this Agreement,' so 'completion' has no fixed moment. That is a specific defect in the trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4.B (c017) is expressly an ongoing, attrition-driven process capped at 370 with a 270 floor; hanging the effective date of the guarantees on its 'completion' cannot be reconciled cleanly with that structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In a position that is within the scope of the present NMDU bargaining unit' uses 'present' without a fixed reference date, and the survival sentence is stated flatly. Nameable but modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the provision 'shall survive the expiration of this Agreement,' which sits against Appendix A, E (c059, c060) terminating guarantees on permanent suspension or termination of employment, and against the different rule for Attachment 2 employees in c055.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until the expiration date of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement' is genuinely two-way: the CBA expiring March 30, 1993, or that agreement as extended to March 30, 2000. The whole duration of the guarantee turns on which is meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble (c001) extends 'the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, which expires on March 30, 1993, until March 30, 2000,' so the instrument itself uses the same phrase for a document with two possible end dates; c054's contrasting survival rule sharpens the problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Utilize fully the services of Guaranteed Employees before employing any additional employees' combined with utilisation 'in inverse seniority order' is odd on its face — inverse seniority ordinarily disfavours the junior — and 'utilize fully' is unquantified. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4.D (c019) gives bidding rights 'by seniority,' while the vacancy side letter (c076) also assigns on an 'inverse seniority basis'; the interaction of straight and inverse seniority across the instrument is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rule is exclusive ('only those individuals listed') with an exception whose members are identified by cross-reference rather than by list, which leaves the excepted class' entitlement undefined. Nameable general-versus-specific tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4.B (c017) says Group I employees promoted through replacement 'shall have a length of contract employment guarantee governed by the terms of Appendix A,' but Appendix A defines its beneficiaries by Attachments 1 and 2 (c051) — a circular fit that a court would have to work out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Suspension turns on circumstances 'under which RSH's are not entitled to be paid under the Collective Bargaining Agreement,' importing an external standard and leaving 'delivery department's operations are suspended' undefined in scope. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The condition depends on the extended CBA under c001 rather than on anything in this instrument, and it sits alongside the permanent-suspension rule in c059; the two are complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Permanent suspension of the Newspaper' uses an undefined subject ('the Newspaper,' not the defined 'The Times') and a vague event; whether a suspension is 'permanent' can only be judged after the fact. Both are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts off guarantees that c054 says 'shall survive the expiration of this Agreement,' so the two duration rules have to be ranked against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An open-ended catch-all — 'for any reason, including but not limited to, retirement, resignation, discharge, death and permanent disability' — where the inclusion of 'discharge' lets one party end the guarantee by its own act. That is a classic list-scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the guarantee in c052 and the survival clause in c054, and nothing in the instrument conditions 'discharge' on cause, so the guarantee's practical content depends on reading these together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination is optional ('may be terminated at the option of The Times') and conditioned on a violation continuing 'notwithstanding the issuance of a temporary restraining order by a court after a hearing' — layered conditions whose sequencing is arguable. Nameable but not extreme.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 7.C (c027) releases the Union from the no-strike obligation in specified circumstances, yet this clause lets The Times end all guarantees for 'any violation of that No-Strike clause' without excepting a released strike; that is a real reconciliation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The me-too right is hedged by two vague provisos — increases 'granted in exchange for productivity improvements or attrition exceeding that which is contained in' the Memorandum, or 'diverted from an existing or subsequently negotiated wage package' — and by a closed parenthetical list of nine unions that raises an expressio unius question. Several nameable soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs through March 30, 2000 and so overlaps the wage reopener and arbitration in paragraph 8 (c032) and the reapportionment mechanism (c033); which route governs 1996-2000 wages is not resolved by the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single concrete undertaking to file papers 'promptly upon notification' of ratification; only 'promptly' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An identical letter appears twice in the instrument, but the duplicate is word-for-word consistent and ratification is defined by paragraph 9 (c035); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All references to "new and rebuilt facilities"' is a sweeping exclusion turning on 'and/or' and on 'the staging facility,' a facility never identified anywhere in the instrument. The undefined referent is precisely nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves directly into paragraphs 1.A, 1.B and 1.C (c002-c004), which are drafted around 'any new or rebuilt facility,' and it interacts with the Carlstadt-to-43rd-Street transfers contemplated by the transition committee letter (c072). Whether the Memorandum's terms apply at 43rd Street after those transfers is genuinely open.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Forty (40) of the current Saturday Night Bulldog finishing times will be assigned to the forty (40) remaining routes' does not say which forty or by what method, and 'the duration of this contract' is undated. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 6 (c021) says the reorganisation is 'subject only to' the forty-route minimum, and c022 caps SNBD start times at 4:00 p.m. after Edison opens; freezing finishing times adds a limit paragraph 6 says does not exist and lengthens shifts fixed by c022.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shortfalls that may exist between shift contributions needed to maintain benefits status' and 'necessary to maintain benefit status' import an external, changing plan standard with no formula; the obligation's size is undeterminable from the text. That is a nameable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3.A.(3) (c011) says its contributions are 'in lieu of and not in addition to those that would otherwise be called for,' while this letter requires 'additional contributions' beyond 3.A.(3) when it is insufficient; that is a direct pull between two operative texts on the same fund.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Separate contributions' of unstated amount to fund 'shortfalls' measured against 'shift contributions needed to maintain benefit status' leaves the pension obligation open-ended. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 3.A.(5) (c013) and the reapportionment cap of 15.68% in c033: whether these separate pension contributions count toward that cap is unaddressed, and c068 conditions them on employee conduct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole funding obligation is conditioned on the 'willingness of the individuals involved to avail themselves of all work opportunities that may exist at The New York Times' — 'willingness,' 'all work opportunities' and 'may exist' are each unbounded. Squarely a vagueness problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the welfare and pension shortfall promises in c066 and c067 and interacts with paragraph 4.C (c018), under which The Times need not offer replacement work; individual willingness may never be testable if no work is offered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is arithmetically odd: the minimum FTE contribution is 450, yet it is increased 'by a number equal to the number of FTE's employed in excess of 370,' so employment of 400 would yield a 480 minimum. The mismatch between the 450 base and the 370 trigger is a nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly amends paragraph 3-A(3) (c011), whose floor is 450 FTEs, while paragraph 4.A (c016) uses 370 as the RSH headcount target and c074 reduces the same 450-FTE obligation for 1996 payments; the three adjustments to one contribution figure do not obviously cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Dedicated school and college routes may be added as needed,' suspension 'e.g., during summer and school holidays, or abolished at the discretion of The Times' pairs an illustrative list with unfettered discretion, and the start time 'will revert to 11:30 p.m.' without saying for how long. Nameable list-and-discretion tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates route and shift rules outside the reorganisation paragraphs (c020, c021) and outside the tailman staffing assumptions there ('such routes will not require a tailman'); the fit is loose but I found no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will make every effort within its control to insure that the NMDU's jurisdiction ... is protected' is a best-efforts promise with no standard, and 'bootlegging' is never defined. Both are nameable and the clause may be aspirational only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers jurisdiction to 'the Collective Bargaining Agreement' extended by c001 rather than defining it here; nothing else in the instrument addresses bootlegging, so no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete deadline and a fixed committee composition; only the phrase 'the appropriate workforce' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates transfers to 43rd Street, which the new-and-rebuilt-facilities letter (c064) excludes from the Memorandum's facility provisions; the two touch but do not clearly conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Specifically charged with administering the transfer process' states a remit without any decision-making power, deadlines or deadlock rule. Mildly vague but short and unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds nothing beyond c072 and does not displace the vacancy-filling procedures in the separate side letter (c076-c080); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanism is internally awkward: contributions made in calendar year 1996 reduce an obligation, and 'said reductions will be evenly distributed throughout the calendar years 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995' — a retroactive spreading of a figure not knowable until 1996. That is a concrete drafting defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3-A(3) (c011) fixes a minimum of 450 FTEs for 1992-1995 and says nothing about 1996, while side letter c069 increases the same figure and c066 requires additional contributions; the four texts adjust one obligation in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to take unspecified 'steps necessary to effectuate amendments' — an agreement to agree, with no standard for what amendments are 'necessitated.' Mildly nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly serves paragraph 3-A(3) (c011) and the same letter (c074); it is facilitative rather than in tension with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'On an inverse seniority basis, to assign the most junior qualified situation holder' leaves 'qualified' undefined and 'pending final award' undated, and the sentence describes both parties as agreeing to assign. Nameable but modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be squared with c078, which requires the Chapel Chairman volunteer step 'prior to instituting the procedure above,' and with the seniority bidding rights in 4.D (c019) and inverse-seniority utilisation in Appendix A, C (c056).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph says junior holders 'shall be restored to their former situation' at the end of a temporary situation and then that they 'shall be permanently assigned to permanent or vacant positions in the event those situations are not filled by bid' — two outcomes for the same person without a stated priority. That is a nameable internal tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same permanent-assignment rule reappears in c078's closing sentence with the added consequence that 'the volunteer shall return to his regular situation'; the two statements of the rule are not identically framed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sequencing is confusing — a volunteer must be supplied and must fill the situation within seven days, yet the vacancy is then permanently assigned to the most junior qualified holder 'in the event the situation is not filled by bid,' with no rule for when a volunteer has filled it. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says it must occur 'prior to instituting the procedure above,' which reverses the order in which c076 and c077 are written, and it duplicates c077's permanent-assignment sentence with a different consequence for the volunteer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any temporary vacancy which is foreseen to be of two (2) weeks or less duration' turns on who foresees and when, and there is no rule for a vacancy that overruns the forecast. That is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It exempts the procedures in c076-c078 without saying what applies instead to short vacancies; the gap is a loose end rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The option to fill any vacancies created as a result of the assignment' is a plain discretionary right, though 'option' leaves the alternative unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with 4.D (c019), under which vacated situations may be filled or eliminated at The Times' discretion subject to manning requirements; the two are broadly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The NMDU may, within 72 hours, discuss the possibility of employment opportunities' creates at most a right to talk, with the 72 hours running from an unspecified point and no obligation on The Times. The provision may be argued to promise nothing at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument addresses hiring from other newspapers, and it does not touch the RSH list mechanics in paragraph 4 (c016, c017); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named individual, a named position, fixed days off and a fixed start time; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a one-off settlement that does not engage the bidding, seniority or vacancy provisions elsewhere in the instrument in any obvious way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite undertaking to withdraw a grievance with prejudice, with the consideration recited. Plain words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the counterpart of c082 and does not bear on the grievance and arbitration machinery in paragraph 2 (c005-c007); no conflict found.
